trust_decision.summary: HTMLParser.goahead decides, when close() forces EOF on an unterminated '<' construct, how far to consume; pre-fix it consumed only to the next '>'/'<' and rescanned (quadratic); the fix consumes to end of buffer and reports per HTML5 EOF rules. At the pinned commit this fix is ALREADY PRESENT.

landing_point.why: Summary names HTMLParser and malformed input; the 'if k < 0: if not end' EOF branch of goahead is the only place incomplete constructs are handled at close().

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Lib/_markupbase.py:60 and Lib/_markupbase.py:141 (parse_declaration/parse_marked_section) are not called by HTMLParser at the pinned commit (only a comment at Lib/html/parser.py:323), so they are not a route

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route found; nothing to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unterminated comments, CDATA, doctype and PIs at EOF must still be reported through handle_comment/unknown_decl/handle_decl/handle_pi, and a lone '<' or '</' must still be emitted as data; dropping the tail or erroring breaks these

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parse_pi returning -1 on missing '>' with an EOF branch that rescans only to the next '>' instead of consuming the rest
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Each construct has its own EOF branch at Lib/html/parser.py:240-263; a maintainer could special-case PIs like the pre-fix code did.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: '&#' with no charref match consumes only two characters then breaks, the same rescan-the-tail idiom
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Entity/charref tail handling sits in the same goahead loop and uses the same partial-consume pattern. Its complexity at the pinned commit was not checked.

O9_family: CWE-1333 / CWE-407 algorithmic complexity (quadratic rescanning of unterminated markup at EOF)

O10_build.language: Python (stdlib module inside the CPython C tree)
O10_build.toolchain: C compiler + make to build CPython 3.10 (./configure && make); the module is pure Python

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Cap the EOF rescan or skip to the next '>' once, instead of consuming the whole tail and reporting it according to HTML5 EOF rules.
